# Objective

This project investigates **genomic prediction using regularized artificial
neural networks**, with emphasis on whether L1 and L2 weight penalties improve
predictive performance relative to an unregularized ANN and to a conventional
genomic mixed model.

The study contains two complementary branches:

1. controlled simulated genomic scenarios, in which the true genetic value is
   known and can be used for independent predictive assessment;
2. a real *Coffea arabica* dataset, used to evaluate the models under an
   applied breeding context.

# Model comparison

The canonical model set is:

- `GBLUP_ADE`;
- `ANN_0`;
- `ANN_L1`;
- `ANN_L2`;
- `ANN_L1_L2`, displayed as **ANN-L1+L2**.

All ANN variants use the same multilayer-perceptron implementation. They differ
only in the coefficients applied to the L1 and L2 penalties on network weights.
Bias terms are not penalized.

The ANN objective function is

\[
\mathrm{MSE}
+\lambda_1\sum_j |w_j|
+\frac{\lambda_2}{2}\sum_j w_j^2.
\]

The combined L1+L2 model is therefore described explicitly as simultaneous L1
and L2 neural-network weight regularization.

# Simulated genomic data

The simulated branch contains six scenarios that form a **genetic-complexity
gradient**. The scenarios differ in genetic architecture and nominal
heritability. Because the design is not a complete factorial combination of
number of QTL and heritability, global changes across all six scenarios are not
interpreted as the isolated causal effect of either factor.

Within equal-heritability pairs, comparisons can be made more directly between
different levels of genetic complexity.

# Real coffee data

The real-data branch uses coffee genotype and phenotype information. Genotype
quality control and phenotype adjustment are treated as separate analytical
steps. The provenance of the adjusted phenotypes is audited against the
available raw multi-year phenotypic records before genomic prediction.

# Validation and tuning

All models are evaluated using common held-out partitions. ANN
hyperparameters are selected only within the outer-analysis data. The
outer-assessment sample is reserved for predictive evaluation.

The public simulated-data workflow contains a **single canonical ANN
analysis**. Hyperparameter tuning is an internal stage of that workflow rather
than a separate public analysis page. Development sensitivity, boundary, and
convergence diagnostics were used to establish and validate the final ANN
protocol; their methodological conclusions are incorporated into the canonical
analysis and those development modules are not part of the public workflow.

Training epochs are treated as a fixed optimization protocol rather than a
scientific tuning dimension. The canonical protocol distinguishes between:

- hyperparameters selected by inner cross-validation;
- fixed optimization controls such as maximum training epochs and patience;
- final model refitting on the full outer-analysis sample.

# Reproducible research

The project is implemented in R with **workflowr**. Source analysis pages are
stored under `analysis/`, rendered website files under `docs/`, and reusable
analysis objects under `output/`.

The workflow is designed so that routine rendering of the website does not
automatically rerun computationally expensive model fitting.
